key_insight: OceanCoder uses engineering verification as a training signal to improve automated ocean-engineering simulation modelling beyond syntactic correctness and successful execution.
engineering_relevance: It targets expert-intensive model construction by checking task constraints, required analyses and the engineering plausibility of simulation outputs.
method: Fine-tune Qwen3-8B on 12,000 verified examples spanning 12 engineering task categories.
Apply three-layer verification to model inputs, analysis completion and output plausibility.
Use graded verification rewards for group relative policy optimisation (GRPO).
evidence_signal: On a benchmark covering out-of-distribution tasks and real-world engineering cases, reported Pass@1 rose from 0% for the base model to 46.77% after supervised fine-tuning and 51.43% after GRPO.
watch_item: A 51.43% Pass@1 leaves substantial failure risk; verification coverage and expert review remain important before engineering deployment.
paper_title: OceanCoder: A Verification-Guided Large Language Model for Automated Simulation Modelling in Ocean Engineering
